# Vim cheatsheet

*Generated by `tools/gen-keymap-docs.js` from `VIM_BINDINGS` in
`src/editor/vim.js` — do not edit by hand. `npm test` fails when this file
drifts, and the same table is exercised by `tests/unit/vim.test.js`.*

Vim mode is on by default (`editor.vimMode`); turning it off switches to the
modeless keymap in [`keymap.md`](./keymap.md). **Ctrl+C always quits** and
**Ctrl+K always opens the palette**, in every mode.

## Two deliberate differences from standard vim

1. **The caret is a boundary.** It may sit one column past the last
   character, so a range is `[start, end)` rather than inclusive. That is why
   a bare `v` followed by `d` deletes nothing (vim deletes one character),
   and why a one-column block needs `<C-v>jd` to mean "the column the caret
   is on" — the corner moves one column further out to include it.
2. **A search starts strictly after the caret**, so `/x` with the caret on an
   `x` moves to the next one — that is what lets `n` advance.

`:w` and its friends are registry commands, not editor functions: `:w`
checks your code because `challenge.check` does. Substitute replacements do
not expand backreferences (`\1` lands literally).
